input.quote: The parties agree that all drawings, documents, designs, models, inventions, computer programs, computer systems, data, computer documentation and other tangible materials authored or prepared by Contractor for Company as the work product required by a Statement of Work (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
input.rationale: Direction of ownership runs our way and the rule's material terms are met at or above the preferred position: § 4(a) vests all Works (deliverables/work product under each SOW) in Clear Capital as Company, with Contractor obliged to execute further documents to perfect those rights (p0018); § 4(b) confirms Contractor merely retains its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies and know-how (a permitted vendor carve-out); and § 4(c) grants us a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify, create derivative versions of and display any Contractor's Information embedded in the Works for our business operations — i.e. the licence-back the preferred position requires. There is no assignment of our IP or data to Contractor, no joint ownership, and § 5(b) expressly excepts programs, data and materials we provide from Contractor's conveyance, while § 8 treats our data as our Confidential Information usable only to perform the Services. Sub-elements short of the ideal drafting, noted but not flagged: ownership of Works is expressed as vesting for periods invoiced and paid (and § 4(d) ties unrestricted modification/re-engagement of third parties to payment in full or termination), the § 4(c) licence is not expressly stated to be irrevocable or worldwide, and there is no standalone "Customer Data remains ours" sentence. We would tidy these in negotiation if the document opens for other reasons, but none defeats the fallback, so no redline.
